subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Obtain the parametric equations of the circle 4(x² + y²) = 9.

insider_note: Dividing by 4 first is the whole question: 9/4 is r², so the radius is 3/2 and not 9/4 — squaring and un-squaring at the wrong moment is the only way to go wrong here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Divide to the standard form
steps.margin_note: One mark. Divide by 4 so the coefficient of x² is 1, then read 9/4 as r².
steps.memory_tip: x² + y² = r². Whatever sits on the right is r squared, not r.
steps.why: The standard form needs coefficient 1 on x² and y². After dividing, the right side is r², so the radius is its square root.
common_mistakes: Dividing only the left side by 4.

steps.label: Write the parametric equations
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The centre is the origin, so there is nothing to add in front.
steps.memory_tip: Centre at the origin: x = r cos θ and y = r sin θ, with nothing added.
lines: Here g = 0 and f = 0, so the centre is the origin.
x = r cos θ,  y = r sin θ

lines.text: ∴ x = (3/2) cos θ,  y = (3/2) sin θ

steps.why: With the centre at the origin the constant parts vanish and the parametric form is the plain r cos θ and r sin θ.
common_mistakes: Adding a centre term that is not there.
